metadata.name: origin.io
metadata.description: Origin lifecycle effect channel. An origin-application's slot FormulaCels (<app>.open/.edit/.new/.save/.load/.close and an origin-user's <seg>.flush) evaluate to a {op,…} descriptor and emit here; the stateful drain executes it via the user-space ops. Formulas never touch state — the descriptor is pure, the drain holds state.

metadata.name: origin.io.drain
metadata.description: (items) — interpret origin lifecycle descriptors with state: new→newUserSpace, save→saveUserSpace, open→hydrate-closure, close→closeUserSpace, load→sha/compat gate then loadUserSpace, flush→optional save (the kernel evicts). Composition over the shipped user-space ops; no new persistence.

metadata.name: origin.new
metadata.description: (app, name) → {op:'new'} descriptor. Use in an origin-application's .new slot; emits to origin.io, the drain creates the origin-user segment.

metadata.name: origin.save
metadata.description: (name) → {op:'save'} descriptor. Use in a .save slot; the drain persists the origin-user's private closure via saveUserSpace/store.put.

metadata.name: origin.load
metadata.description: (name, version?) → {op:'load'} descriptor. The drain runs the sha/compat gate, then loadUserSpace (which auto-starts the parent application).

metadata.name: origin.open
metadata.description: (app) → {op:'open'} descriptor — open the origin-application standalone (no user-segment). The drain hydrates the app closure.

metadata.name: origin.close
metadata.description: (name) → {op:'close'} descriptor — close an origin-user segment (closeUserSpace flushes its private closure root-first).

metadata.name: origin.flush
metadata.description: (name, save?) → {op:'flush'} descriptor for an origin-user's <seg>.flush slot. The kernel flush hook enqueues this BEFORE eviction; the drain optionally saves first (close ≠ save), then the kernel evicts the cels.

metadata.name: origin.fire
metadata.description: (slotKey) — discrete dispatcher: enqueue a slot cel's current descriptor to its declared channel(s) and drain origin.io. The host calls this on a user action (save/open/new/load/close); the kernel flush hook is the equivalent trigger for the flush slot.
